newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lan Chile expects 50pct ex-Europe cargo growth.
newsitem.headline: Lan Chile expects 50pct ex-Europe cargo growth.

text.p: Lan Chile foresees up to a 50 percent growth in its European air cargo exports to South America this year, after more than tripling volumes in 1995, said cargo manager Europe, Martin Rehs.
He said exports should reach 2,950 tonnes this year, compared to 2,012 tonnes last year and 616 tonnes in 1994.
"In the first half of 1996 we exceeded by far the sales of the first half of 1995," he told Reuters in an interview .
"This is because we are using special freighters on charter and we are seeking to use interline opportunities more," he added.
Up to 80 percent of European freight originates in Germany and the remainder is trucked to Frankfurt from the Netherlands, Britain and France, while Spanish cargo is trucked to Madrid, he said.
Frankfurt-based Rehs, said Lan Chile achieves cargo load factors of 95-100 percent on passenger services in the high season and 85-100 percent in the low season.

Capacity from Europe has increased with the doubling of Frankfurt-Madrid-Santiago passenger flights to four and because of upgrading B767-200 aircraft to B767-300ER aircraft, over the last two years, he noted.
The airline has also increased its average tonnage per flight by improving sales co-ordination between general sales agents in Germany, Spain, the Netherlands, Britain and France, he said.
Although each gsa has fixed allotments, Frankfurt decides which consignments will go on which flights to maximise loads, he said.
Rehs, cargo manager Europe since the start of 1995, said he appointed Air Logistics as the UK gsa and Chapman Freeborn for Spain at the start of this year.
Lan Chile plans to expand into the Italian market from October, he added.
